range_state.list: 環境省レッドリスト2020 (貝類)
range_state.assessment_basis: Ministry of the Environment Japan red-list categories, which name their IUCN equivalent (準絶滅危惧 = NT)
range_state.continuity: NT in the 2015, 2017, 2018 and 2019 mollusc lists (as Crassostrea sikamea) and in 2020 (as Magallana sikamea); each CSV read 2026-10-02
range_state.limitations: A national assessment of Japan, where the species is confined to the Ariake and northern Yatsushiro seas; not an IUCN global or Korean assessment. In Korea it is known from few sites (Hong et al. 2012, Fish Sci 78:259). Never ranked or pooled with IUCN-based or Korean national MCUI.

range_state.list: Красная книга Российской Федерации (растения и грибы), Section 5 ВОДОРОСЛИ, row 594
range_state.assessment_basis: The list's threat-status column uses the IUCN codes defined in Order No. 306 para 3.7 (as amended 2020): 'У - Уязвимые (VU - Vulnerable)'. The rarity column ('3 - Редкие') is a Russian scale and is not mapped.
range_state.continuity: Row 635 of the 2005 list (Order No. 289) already held Gelidium elegans at rarity category 3; that list had no threat-status column, so the VU reading is first stated in the 2023 list.
range_state.limitations: Russia is the northern edge of the range (Amur Bay and Cape De-Friz, Peter the Great Gulf) and the species is recorded there as single finds, so this is a peripheral-population assessment, not a range-wide one. Japan, the centre of the range, does not list the species in the Ministry of the Environment algae red lists of 2020 or 2025 (the congener Gelidium hirsutum is listed); absence from a threatened-species list is not an LC assessment and does not overturn the Russian category. Never ranked or pooled with IUCN-based or Korean national MCUI.
